t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup: a warm limestone paper sheet inset on a deep navy page with a narrow navy margin and a thin top bar holding a wordmark and section label. On the sheet, an oversized two-line light-weight sans-serif headline in sentence case fills the top half, with a light subhead below. Left: numbered entries in a ruled grid, each with a mono numeral, a mono uppercase title and short body text for <CONTENT>, divided by hairline rules. Right: a large navy hairline isometric line drawing of a pipe frame with elbows. Flat, square corners, no shadows, calm and spacious.
signature_idea: A giant light headline and a quiet isometric pipe drawing share one limestone sheet, with the package laid out as a numbered ruled index beneath.
strengths: light oversized headline, mono numerals and limestone-on-navy are on-brand
numbered ruled grid is a clear, buildable index for a document package
line drawing gives equipment context without colour or noise
lots of space, calm and readable
weaknesses: headline is not cropped by the frame, so the editorial drama is mild
grid is irregular: entry 03 sits alone with an empty cell below and vertical rules end at uneven lengths
pipe drawing is a generic pipe rack with odd floating fittings, not a recognisable skid
no steel-blue accent, so nothing marks focus
entry text is dense small body copy
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone, a light sans headline, mono numerals, hairline navy line art, square corners and generous space match the brand book closely.
